description: Final taxonomically harmonised species name from a taxonomic backbone such as WCVP or GBIF.
Family name as the GBIF backbone accepts it. Given beside wcvp_family because the two backbones place some families differently and neither is silently preferred.
Genus name as the GBIF backbone accepts it.
Plant order from the GBIF backbone, filled for 99.7% of matched names. This is the order to group or filter on.
Species name as the GBIF backbone accepts it.
How the source name met the GBIF backbone: the match status GBIF returned, such as accepted or synonym.
GBIF backbone usage key for the matched name, for linking out to GBIF.
Original species name reported by the primary source, when available.
Species name or accepted/source-resolved name supplied by the downloaded secondary dataset, when available.
Plant family name reported by the source or added during taxonomy matching.
Plant genus name reported by the source or added during taxonomy matching.
Plant order name as the source reported it. Filled for about a third of records and the sources disagree with each other, so it is provenance only - group and filter on gbif_order instead.
Family name as WCVP accepts it.
Genus name as WCVP accepts it.
Species name as WCVP (World Checklist of Vascular Plants) accepts it.
How the source name met WCVP: an exact match, a match to a synonym resolved to the accepted name, or a fuzzy match.
Primary reference, citation, DOI, or source-reference field reported in the dataset.
Folder/source identifier for the downloaded dataset.
File within the source folder that the record was read from.

Quality flag on a numeric value, which is kept, not removed: unit_factor (the value differs from the species' other values by almost exactly x10, x100, x1000 or x25.4, the signature of a unit or per-100/per-1000-seeds slip) and/or trait_extreme (outside the 0.1-99.9 percentile of all values of the trait). Empty when neither applies. Species summaries use medians, so a flagged value barely moves them.

Identifier of this row, EB_1 .. EB_n, assigned once when the dataset is finished. One row, one id. It follows row order, so it is stable only while the dataset is not regenerated; record_id_crosswalk.csv.gz is what re-links ids to rows after a rebuild.
Number of individuals, observations or replicates behind the value, when the source states it. Needed to weight a mean and to convert a standard error to a standard deviation.
Folder holding the source dataset, as organised in this database.

What the value is: a single or unspecified value, a mean, median, minimum, maximum, standard deviation (sd), standard error (se), or a sample size (n). A value marked sd or se is a dispersion, not a measurement.

Whether the number is in the trait's standard unit: converted_or_already_target (it is), unit_missing (the source stated no unit and the value is assumed to be in the standard unit), needs_unit_check (the unit could not be resolved, so the value is as the source gave it), not_applicable (the trait has no unit).
Diaspore or dispersal-unit color name or categorical color class.
Dry mass or dry weight of the diaspore or dispersal unit.
Diaspore or dispersal-unit length.
Diaspore or dispersal-unit thickness/height; spelling follows the reviewed TRY fine-trait audit label.
Diaspore or dispersal-unit type.
Diaspore or dispersal-unit width.
Derived broad dispersal category for dispersal_mode records: biotic, abiotic, or autochorous.
Continuous seed or fruit dispersal distance.
Categorical or ordinal class describing seed or fruit dispersal distance.
Maximum seed, fruit, or diaspore dispersal distance.
Dispersal-kernel category, function, parameter, or summary descriptor.
Derived dispersal mechanism for dispersal_mode records, describing how the propagule is moved.
Original or first-pass recoded dispersal-mode/syndrome value retained for traceability before hierarchical dispersal scoring.
